dod_intent_evidence: 2022 AF SBIR Phase II ($749,607) to militarize their COTS FlightRisk app with Patriot Excalibur integration and DoD cloud cybersecurity, followed by an Oct 2025 OUSD SBIR to add generative AI capabilities (SBIR/STTR record + News section) — a DoD-specific transition still incomplete three years after Phase II despite a mature commercial product.
score_evidence: 'AI-powered ecosystem that transforms data into actionable insights' → lab_language_intensity (moderate SaaS-marketing buzz, not heavy TRL/demo-brag)

SBIR abstract explicitly names 'the required DoD cyber security for cloud-based software applications' and integration with 'Air Force authoritative data sources (e.g., Patriot Excalibur...)' → deployment_awareness_absence scored low (real compliance/integration awareness)
customer testimonials are literally from chief pilots and safety managers describing daily field use ('iPad when I'm out flying') → operator_absence scored very low
Open roles are Customer Success Specialist and Training and Support Specialist — support/training-skewed, not pure-research hiring → hiring_profile_skew scored low

founded 2007, 2,500+ commercial customers, revenue-generating enterprise SaaS on Azure → stage_pressure scored low (financially stable company, DoD track is a slow-moving side effort not an existential bet)

blind_spots.blind_spot: VOCUS is described as producing 'operational readiness' and risk data 'at all levels' but never mentions ATAK/TAK or any tactical situational-awareness integration.
blind_spots.operator_reality: If Air Force leadership wants pre-flight risk data alongside a unit's broader tactical picture, a system that lives only in its own web/mobile app — not federated into existing C2/SA tools — creates one more login and one more silo commanders have to check separately.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Product architecture and go-to-market are built around the commercial business-aviation safety-manager workflow, where TAK/C2 integration was never a requirement.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: 'Integrated insights directly inform decision-making at all levels.'

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Hosted on Microsoft Azure... enterprise-grade reliability, scalability, and security with >99% uptime' assumes reliable connectivity with no discussion of degraded or disconnected operation at forward or austere aviation sites.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A pre-flight risk assessment tool that can't be trusted to load when a squadron is operating from an austere strip with intermittent SATCOM is exactly the DDIL failure mode the checklist warns about — 99% uptime is a garrison-network number, not a DDIL number.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The company's architecture and pitch are built for the commercial business-aviation market (FBOs, corporate flight departments) where cloud connectivity is a safe assumption.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: 'Hosted on Microsoft Azure, VOCUS delivers enterprise-grade reliability, scalability, and security with >99% uptime.'

blind_spots.blind_spot: No mention of who sustains or administers the DoD-specific version at squadron level once Polaris Aero's own commercial customer-success team isn't the one supporting it.
blind_spots.operator_reality: 'Military unique real-time refresher training aids' and 'post flight reporting and feedback' need someone at the unit to own configuration and troubleshooting when pilot turnover happens — the SBIR abstract names the knowledge-gap problem for pilots but never names who owns the software itself day to day.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Support model (Customer Success Specialist, Training and Support Specialist open roles) is built for commercial B2B SaaS accounts, not garrison-level government IT sustainment.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: 'Pilot turnover is unavoidable in the Air Force... Polaris Aero's proposed solution will fill in the knowledge gap when experienced pilots leave and inexperienced pilots join a new squadron.'

opener_hook: Your 2022 AF Phase II targeted Patriot Excalibur integration and DoD cloud cybersecurity — three years and one more SBIR later, is FlightRisk fielded fleet-wide yet, or still garrison-by-garrison?
what_they_do: Cloud-based aviation safety management and pre-flight risk-assessment SaaS (VOCUS), building a DoD/Air Force-specific AI-enabled variant under SBIR funding on top of an already-mature commercial product.
